vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: dr-context-pipeline
Version: 1.7.0

The dr-context-pipeline skill implements a structured Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework designed to improve agent memory management and observability. The included Python scripts (install_pipeline.py, validate_pipeline.py, and memory_watchdog.py) perform legitimate file synchronization, integrity hashing, and workspace health checks. The instructions in SKILL.md and the Runtime Evidence Checklist (RUNTIME_CHECKLIST.md) enforce a strict 'evidence contract' requiring the agent to output its internal retrieval state as JSON, which serves as a transparency and debugging feature rather than a malicious diversion. No evidence of data exfiltration, unauthorized persistence, or harmful prompt injection was found.

llm.summary: The skill's files, runtime instructions, and requested actions align with its stated purpose (installing and enforcing a local deterministic context/memory pipeline); it operates on local workspace files and does not request credentials or download external code.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (deterministic retrieval + compression pipeline) match the included assets and scripts. The skill asks the agent to install files into a workspace, run local validators/watchdogs, and patch AGENTS.md — all expected for a pipeline that standardizes context loading.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md requires the agent to run the included Python scripts, read and modify local files (context_pipeline/, AGENTS.md, workspace/memory/*) and to paste raw command outputs and JSON artifacts (Retrieval Bundle, Context Pack, snippet texts) into the transcript. This is coherent with the pipeline's evidence contract but has privacy implications because it requires emitting snippet text and file metadata into the conversation.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no network download or external install step; the installer simply copies bundled assets into the workspace (shutil.copytree). No brew/npm/extract-from-URL behavior is present. All code to be executed is included in the skill bundle.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables, credentials, or config paths. Scripts operate on workspace-relative paths and do not attempt to access unrelated secrets or external services.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not request permanent platform-wide privileges. It does instruct the agent to modify the local AGENTS.md and to lay down files under workspace/context_pipeline, which is appropriate for an installable local pipeline. No modifications to other skills' configs or system-wide agent settings are requested.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears internally consistent and does what it says: it installs a local context pipeline and enforces a strict runtime evidence contract. Before enabling or running it, consider the following: (1) The workflow requires the agent to read and emit memory snippets and file contents (memory/* and AGENTS.md) into the transcript — review those files for sensitive data and back them up. (2) The installer copies files into your workspace/context_pipeline and the validator/watchdog reads your workspace/memory; run these scripts in a sandboxed or disposable copy of your workspace if you want to inspect behavior first. (3) Review the three included Python scripts (install_pipeline.py, validate_pipeline.py, memory_watchdog.py) yourself to confirm they meet your policies (they perform local file ops and hashing only; no network calls were found). (4) Because the runtime contract requires pasting Retrieval Bundle and Context Pack JSON (including snippet text), do not apply this skill if you cannot permit those snippets to appear in conversation logs. If you'd like, run the installer and validator manually on a test workspace and confirm outputs before letting the agent execute the apply flow autonomously.
